Thanks for the ping, Sergio — happy to take point on the SOC 2 mapping. Quick answers and action items below (I kept these concise so Nimbus can drop into their intake):

- Customer VPC components (run in-customer):
  * Model inference workers (reserved GPUs) — run in customer VPC on dedicated hosts; no outbound internet access by default; egress restricted to Redwood telemetry endpoints via NAT/proxy when enabled.
  * KV cache sidecar — colocated with inference worker; encrypted in transit; access controlled via mTLS to model process only.
  * Sidecar metrics exporter — pushes metrics to a forwarding proxy; telemetry is buffered locally and sent over an isolated egress channel to Redwood-managed observability.

- Redwood-managed control plane (Redwood-managed infra):
  * Scheduler & orchestration — controls job placement, doesn't see model weights or customer data in plaintext; communicates over mutually authenticated control channel with agents in the customer VPC.
  * Artifact registry & model-store (encrypted at rest) — customer can bring-your-own-encrypted model artifacts or reference public models; access is controlled by KMS policies.
  * Central logging/analytics pipelines — ingest pseudonymized telemetry, access controlled by RBAC and audited.

- Egress/ingress controls & evidence we can attach:
  * VPC ACLs and Security Group screenshots showing restricted CIDR ranges to telemetry endpoints (attach: sg-private-telemetry-screenshot.png).
  * Example VPC Flow Log extract (attach: vpcflow-sample.csv) showing allowed host->telemetry flows only.
  * KMS key policy snippet for model-store (attach: kms-policy-snippet.txt).

SOC 2 mapping (short-form):
- CC6: Logical access controls — model-store access governed by KMS + RBAC; logs retained and audited.
- CC7: System operations and availability — scheduler HA, dedicated capacity SLAs, runbooks for failover documented.

Action items:
1) Karthik: can you confirm there are no control-plane processes that ever mount customer model weights in plaintext? (I believe everything uses encrypted-at-rest + ephemeral decryption only inside the customer's enclave.)
2) Marissa: can you attach the Private onboarding checklist and the standard VPC ACL template Nimbus can use?
3) Sergio: I'll draft the 1–2 line SOC 2 mappings per component and upload the snippets listed above.

Kimberly Park
Director, Product Security
Redwood Inference

Hi Claire — thanks for the quick turnaround. Per Kimberly's notes (below) and Karthik's offline confirmation, here are the deliverables we can provide by EOD Friday for your compliance intake:

Deliverables we will attach to your intake template:
- component_topology_v1.drawio.png — annotated: components in-customer vs Redwood-managed; dataflow arrows labeled with auth/crypto assumptions.
- segregation_matrix_v2.xlsx — mapping of components to SIG questions + residual risk notes.
- soc2_control_map.csv — concise CC6/CC7 mapping lines per component (1–2 sentences each).
- sg-private-telemetry-screenshot.png, vpcflow-sample.csv, kms-policy-snippet.txt (evidence stubs).

Short clarifications for the intake form (you can paste these):
1) Customer data or model inputs are processed within the customer's VPC on dedicated hosts; Redwood's control plane issues jobs and receives only hashed/pseudonymized telemetry unless the customer opts into full observability.
2) No Redwood-managed process mounts customer model weights in plaintext; decryption is ephemeral and keys are customer-controlled via KMS.
3) Default egress from inference hosts is blocked; when telemetry is enabled we use an explicit egress proxy with a narrow allowlist and mutual TLS.

I've uploaded the artifacts to the Drive folder (link above). If Nimbus wants, we can schedule a 30-minute call with Kimberly to walk the SOC 2 mapping live.

Thanks —
Sergio Alvarez
Senior Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
